tool.title: Moorkyz Media Recover
tool.summary: Safely recover and preserve accessible video and audio from connected devices and local folders. Know exactly where every file was saved.
tool.catalogDescription: Give accessible recordings a safer route from your phone or scattered folders to a backup you can trace. This independent Windows desktop preview scans local folders and authorized Android storage, lets you review dates and duplicates, then copies without changing the originals. Retry interrupted files, check saved bytes with SHA-256 and follow per-file reports to their exact destination. It preserves readable media; it does not undelete protected phone data.
tool.description: An independent, offline-first Windows desktop application for recursively discovering accessible audio and video in local folders and authorized Android USB/MTP storage, including Samsung phones. Scan before copying, review date filters and duplicate candidates, then back up without changing originals. Interrupted files can be retried from the beginning, saved bytes checked with SHA-256, and results traced through detailed reports. This page explains the desktop tool; it cannot scan your computer or phone.

howItWorks.title: Choose source
howItWorks.text: Select local folders or an authorized, unlocked portable device, then choose an absolute save folder.

howItWorks.title: Scan
howItWorks.text: Discover media recursively before copying. Review inaccessible folders and partial scans instead of assuming every subtree was readable.

howItWorks.title: Review
howItWorks.text: Check eligible recordings, date exclusions, unknown dates and destination candidates. The default cutoff is October 1, 2026 inclusive; unknown or conflicting dates are included rather than silently lost.

howItWorks.title: Recover
howItWorks.text: Copy readable sources into staging without modifying originals or overwriting unrelated files. Interrupted MTP files restart from byte zero, not a claimed byte-range resume.

howItWorks.title: Verify
howItWorks.text: Check saved lengths and SHA-256, with verification confidence recorded in the manifest. A saved hash detects later byte changes; it does not prove a recording is playable.

howItWorks.title: Open saved folder
howItWorks.text: Read the exact Saved to path, open the saved files and reports, and review failures before considering the backup complete.

features.title: Discovery & filters
features.text: Recursive video/audio discovery, documented date provenance, unknown-date inclusion and safe exclusions for backup output and filesystem links.

features.title: Reliable transfer
features.text: Read-only sources, collision-safe filenames, per-file staging and bounded retry. Device access depends on Windows, USB mode and phone authorization.

features.title: Verification & repair
features.text: Persistent hashes distinguish trusted saved bytes from legacy candidates. Suspect output is preserved, not silently overwritten; independent source comparison provides a different assurance level from local hashing.

features.title: Reports & history
features.text: Durable job records, per-file results, manifests and exact output locations make incomplete work and verification levels visible.

features.title: Privacy & portability
features.text: A separate Windows desktop runtime, without accounts, telemetry, uploads or a public processing service. The portal stays usable when the desktop app is not running.

limitations: Recover means retrying incomplete transfers or reacquiring damaged backups while the source is still readable. It does not mean undeleting inaccessible phone data, bypassing encryption or extracting hidden/private app storage.
Unlock the phone and authorize File Transfer / Android Auto. WPD access, reconnect behavior and metadata vary by device; real Samsung/Android hardware validation is not a release claim.
Hashes establish byte consistency, not media decodability or authenticity. Background work requires the desktop process and accessible storage; it cannot continue through process exit or sleep.
This is an unreleased development preview. Consult the included implementation status and testing documentation for verified behavior and deferred options before using important media.

Runtime acceptance is blocked on the build machine: Windows Application Control rejected unsigned application DLLs (0x800711C7). A self-contained package was produced, but a successful GUI launch and final expanded test run could not be verified. No desktop screenshot or release-readiness claim is available.

Automatic device reconnect/PUID remapping, embedded capture-date parsing, media decoding, cross-identity content deduplication, tray mode and complete technical-message translation are not implemented. Phone transfers and files larger than 4 GiB remain unverified.
useCases: Retry accessible phone recordings after an unstable USB transfer.
Collect audio and video recursively from a deep local folder tree.
Continue a partially completed backup without overwriting unrelated files.
Check previously saved bytes for later corruption using recorded hashes.
Export a traceable archive with per-file outcomes and saved locations.

setup.title: Check Windows prerequisites
setup.text: Targets Windows 10/11 x64. A self-contained portable build includes its .NET runtime; building the source requires the .NET 10 SDK with Windows desktop targeting support. No prerequisite is installed by visiting this page.

setup.title: Prepare an Android source
setup.text: Use a reliable USB data cable, unlock the phone, select File Transfer / Android Auto and authorize this PC. Select accessible internal storage or SD storage; protected app data is not exposed by this tool.

setup.title: Start the desktop application
setup.text: No public executable release is available yet. Build the canonical source in tools/mediarecover within this repository or use a locally verified portable package supplied by its maintainer. Extract the entire package before starting MoorkyzMediaRecover.exe; do not run source text in this viewer.

setup.title: Choose storage and review the scan
setup.text: Keep the source readable and choose a destination with enough space. Settings and the SQLite ledger live under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Moorkyz\MediaRecover. Staging, quarantine and per-run reports live under the destination's .mediarecover folder. Scan, review, then explicitly start recovery.

setup.title: Review the exact saved paths
setup.text: Use the desktop Saved to path and report actions. Keep quarantined files and original recordings until you have reviewed failures. Processing works offline, and no local browser service or portal opt-in is required.

tool.downloadNotice: Not yet released. There is no public EXE or portable ZIP download. Downloads in the Tool section are text source, not an executable release; a local build is not a published release. Nothing is installed, launched or connected by opening this page.

source.notice: Canonical source maintained in tools/mediarecover in Moorky/moorkyz-tools. Edit it in this repository, then refresh SOURCE-PROVENANCE.json to record the allowlisted files' SHA-256 and source tree hash. The ZIP contains buildable source, not a public executable release.
